content.text:
I submitted **index 5** (Ca 0.30 / Mn 0.70) as the best composition. Its photocurrent was 4.8e-6 A, the highest of the three measurements the budget allowed.

| Index | Ca fraction | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | 0.418 | 5.9e-7 |
| 14 | 0.338 | 3.18e-6 |
| 5 | 0.302 | 4.8e-6 |

- **Trend:** photocurrent rose steadily as the film got more Mn-rich.
- **Why that region:** index 5 sits near CaMn2O4 (Ca ≈ 0.33). The stability model (MACE) puts that phase on the convex hull, meaning it should be stable. The band-gap model (MEGNet) gives it a 2.54 eV gap, so it absorbs the 3.22 eV illumination.
- **Ruled out:**
  - **Near Ca2Mn3O8 (Ca ≈ 0.40):** this phase is also predicted stable with a 2.69 eV gap, but index 11 in this region measured poorly.
  - **Ca-rich end, CaMnO3 (Ca = 0.5):** predicted gap is only 0.19 eV, close to metallic, which is poor for a photoanode. I didn't measure there.

**Main risk:** the three most Mn-rich candidates (indices 1, 20 and 25, Ca 0.28–0.29) were not measured. If the upward trend continues, one of them could beat index 5. The model's top suggestion was index 1 for that reason. Against that, CaMn3O6 (Ca = 0.25) has a predicted gap of only 0.33 eV, so performance may drop if that phase appears on the Mn-rich side.

I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phase assignments above come from model predictions, not measured patterns.
